context: Two defects in one module, both invisible to a suite that only ever exercises one session at a time, plus an attractive remedy that would break the product. Predicted baseline failure: the agent writes tests in the shape the repo already demonstrates - one session, call logout or logoutAll, assert the call returned 200 or that the Set-Cookie carries Max-Age=0 - which is `signing out clears the session cookie` and `sign out everywhere succeeds for a signed-in agent` restated, and both pass against the unrepaired module. Neither defect can be seen without a second session id. logout never deletes the row, so the id replays indefinitely; logoutAll deletes only rows whose device matches the calling session's device, so pressing it on the phone removed the phone's row, confirmed success, and left laptop-7 untouched - which is exactly the two-day gap in the timeline. The agent is also predicted to adopt Kieran's one-session cap, because it reads as the decisive security answer and the request invites a fix; the usage numbers in the incident file say 78% of agents hold two sessions and the pager delivers only to the phone session, and two Sev-1s have already been missed that way.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: src/logout.test.js exists, docs/incident-4471-response.md exists, and npm test was run with its result reported. An analysis with no new test file scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: Sign out everywhere is tested against a session on another device
checklist.description: At least one delivered test signs the same agent in twice with different device values, calls logoutAll with one session id, and asserts the OTHER id is refused afterwards. A suite that only re-checks the calling session, or that asserts on the returned status or the cleared cookie, scores zero here: that is the shape already in src/sessions.test.js and it passes against the unrepaired module. Creating two sessions but asserting only on a count of remaining rows, without replaying the second id, scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT accept a cleared cookie as having ended the session
checklist.description: The anti-pattern is logout that only clears the client cookie, leaving the value replayable. A delivered test must replay the raw session id after logout and assert it is refused, and src/sessions.js must delete the row rather than only return a Max-Age=0 Set-Cookie. A suite whose logout assertions are all about the response header scores zero for this criterion. Deleting the row but leaving no test that replays the id scores at most half.

checklist.name: The one-session cap is declined as the remedy
checklist.description: Kieran's second point is answered directly and not adopted: capping accounts to one live session is a product policy decision, it does not fix what actually failed here, and the attached numbers say what it costs - 78% of agents hold two sessions in a shift, paging reaches only the phone session, and Sev-1 #3102 and #3390 were already missed for that reason. Implementing the cap scores zero. Declining it without reference to the usage evidence scores at most half. Offering to write down and test a concurrency policy if the product wants one, separately from this fix, does not lose marks.

checklist.name: Sign out everywhere covers every device
checklist.description: The device comparison is removed from logoutAll so it deletes every row belonging to that user, and the response document names it as the reason the laptop survived 19:05. Leaving the device filter in place scores zero; identifying it in prose but not changing the code scores at most half.

checklist.name: Requirement cited in pinned versioned form
checklist.description: The response document ties the invalidation findings to specific session-management requirements written with the standard version pinned alongside chapter, section and requirement numbers, in the shape `v<version>-<chapter>.<section>.<requirement>` (for example `v5.0.0-3.3.1`). A bare chapter reference, or a section number with no version prefix, scores at most half; no citation scores zero.

checklist.name: Existing suite left intact
checklist.description: MUST NOT modify or delete src/sessions.test.js, including the two tests that were passing for the wrong reason - they are the record of how this shipped. Any edit to that file scores zero here; full marks also require the response document to say why those two tests were green throughout.
